issues.on_page: Licenses, permits and fees 6,177,633 (Papillion Landing column 2,424,965, Papio Bay 341,376)
issues.issue: Mixed label kept as licenses and permits (allowed: no exact printed breakdown). But the Papillion Landing and Papio Bay columns are what their budget schedules (p11, p12) print as Charges for services, and detail[44]/detail[51] put them in Recreation Fees. The same money is in two different categories at the two levels.
Mixed investment and interest label put in Interest Income; detail_category on the matching detail lines is investment income. Defensible, but it is a judgment call.
The Total-column line includes Golf charges of 2,310,614, which the per-fund detail (detail[88]) classes as Recreation Fees, so the two levels disagree.

issues.on_page: Gain/(Loss) on sale of capital assets 353,475 (Water (2,728), Golf 356,203)
issues.issue: This is a net gain/loss, not sale proceeds; the cash flow statement (p7) shows Golf's gain is mostly a noncash gain on trade-in (358,800). A gain/loss category (e.g. Loss on Disposal of Assets, as for Scottsbluff) may fit better. Same applies to detail[63] and detail[91].
The source of this receipt is not printed; state aid is an assumption (also detail[12]).
The grantor is not printed; state aid is an assumption (also detail[17]).
Assumed to be a reimbursement for fuel; it could also be charges for services (also detail[9]).
Cable TV receipts are assumed to be a franchise fee; the label alone does not say so (also detail[16]).
A keno tax paid by the city could take Other Taxes Paid rather than miscellaneous expenditure.

issues.on_page: Total column cost-type lines include Golf and Business Park amounts
issues.issue: The Total-column business-type spending lines all carry function utilities, but the per-fund detail gives Golf culture/recreation and Business Park economic development. Minor inconsistency.
